newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Central Bank crushes peso attack.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Central Bank crushes peso attack.

text.p: The Philippine peso recovered lost ground on Wednesday after the Central Bank flooded the market with millions of dollars and raised its rate to quell a speculative attack after the Thai baht tumble, traders said.
The Central Bank was forced to protect the peso after Thailand's de facto devaluation on Wednesday.
"I've never seen such an amount changing hands in this market," a foreign banker said as total volume shot to a record $1.049 billion at the close of trading.
The peso ended 26.376 after reaching a low of 26.380.
Traders said the Central Bank sold about $539 million at 26.379 and 26.377, mostly in the morning.
Later, it bought back about $218 million at 26.376 and 26.377 for settlement tomorrow and at 26.368 to 26.370 for delivery today.
Traders said foreign banks unloaded some of the dollars they bought in the morning after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate by nine percentage points to 24 percent.
"Today, the Central Bank successfully quashed the attack on the peso. Tomorrow will be another day, depending on developments in Thailand," said one trader.
